name: Jubilee (Machine Agency, University of Washington)
subcategory: open-source tool-changing motion platform (3D printing, plotting, lab automation)
origin_detail: Designed by Joshua Vasquez of Machine Agency at the University of Washington; the source repository was created on 3 Oct 2019. A companion project, science-jubilee (MIT licence), adapts the platform for lab automation with pipette, syringe and camera tools.
openness_notes: Design files under CC BY 4.0 and described in the README as OSHWA-certified open-source hardware; science-jubilee software under MIT. Scored 3 rather than 4 because development is led by one university lab (community uses Discord and a subreddit; no formal community governance found).

license_history.license: CC BY 4.0 (hardware design files); OSHWA certified per README

risk_events: Main hardware repository last pushed 12 May 2024, suggesting core design development has slowed; activity has shifted to tools and science-jubilee.
Single named kit vendor (Filastruder frame kit, from Feb 2022), so builders largely source parts themselves.
robustness: Fully published design (466 commits, 630 stars, 126 forks) that anyone can build for about $1,350 per unit excluding tools; survives independently of the lab, but has a small commercial supply chain.
physical_science_relevance: A low-cost, open tool-changing gantry that labs use as a configurable self-driving-lab platform (liquid handling, imaging, sample preparation), complementing closed commercial liquid handlers.
openness_effect_assessment: Open, certified designs let other labs adapt Jubilee for chemistry and materials automation (science-jubilee), at a fraction of the cost of commercial robots. Without a company or foundation behind it, supply and maintenance rest on individual builders and one university group.
key_takeaway: Jubilee shows the academic open-hardware route into self-driving labs: a university-designed, OSHWA-certified toolchanger that labs can build for about $1,350, with almost no commercial ecosystem. It is cheap and adaptable but thin on long-term maintenance and supply.
